dimension_justifications.soundness: The internal arithmetic is unusually clean: every headline ratio I recomputed from the tables reproduces exactly (136.235/9.661 = 14.10x; 136.235/34.683 = 3.93x; (140.34-15.89)/140.34 = 88.68%; (4.901-2.229)/4.901 = 54.5%; 20,992x10 = 209,920 and 20,992x30 + 192x30 = 635,520; 8x3x6 = 144, 8x3x540 = 12,960, 8x480 = 3,840; 20+24 = 44 clean and 44 controls), and the claims are hedged with unusual discipline. But three substantive gaps reduce confidence. (1) The system validated in Section 5.5 is not the system measured in Sections 5.2-5.4: Section 5.5 (p.7) and Table 3 (p.14) specify vLLM-0.26 Triton attention with BF16 KV explicitly labelled 'not quantization', 128-token pages, PG-19 4,095-token documents and 8 output tokens, with no split depth, no boundary residual and no dequantization step, whereas Tables 1-2 measure a j=7 quantized Q4/Q4/Q8 split-replay path on Qasper/2WikiMQA. The ownership discipline of Section 4.3 is therefore never validated on the configuration whose numbers the paper reports. (2) The headline capacity/quality result rests on a single archival run that the authors state (p.8, Appendix A) used a mutable code directory with neither a pre-run source ledger nor a model-weight ledger, so it is not regenerable even by the authors. (3) All latency evidence is n=8, medians only, one stack, no dispersion across the three repeats. The claims that are made are mostly supported; the claim the paper's own structure builds toward is not.
dimension_justifications.presentation: Top-level organization is genuinely good and I want to credit it: Section 5 opens with an explicit roadmap, Sections 5.2/5.3/5.4/5.5 are titled by result type so memory, latency, quality and ownership are each findable without hunting, and Section 3's three bolded run-in headers form a real argument that forward-maps explicitly to Sections 4.1-4.4. Below that level the presentation materially obstructs evaluation. Section 5.5 collapses into a wall of unanchored counts ('8x3x6 = 144 selected-owner-row checks, 8x3x540 = 12,960 full serializer/live-object rows... Here 60 = 30x2 denotes persistent layer/family coordinates and 480 = 8x60...') with no main-text table, burying the one finding the abstract leads with; its '0/5 ... 1/5' statistic has an ambiguous antecedent that points readers at the wrong campaign. The two main tables cannot be cross-read: only three of six rows are common, the same policy carries four different names with two different Store values, and the same nominal full-prefix Q16 baseline is 136.235 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 140.34 MiB/doc in Table 2 with no reconciliation. Both main tables carry entirely empty columns for a metric ('Recall') that is never defined anywhere in 31 pages. Figure 3 is never cited; Tables 3 and 4 are never cited and have no lead-in prose; Table 4's caption invokes an undefined internal tag 'V29'. The split depth that determines Eq. 2 appears only inside a figure caption. Sections 1 and 3 are roughly half redundant and together consume more main text than Sections 5.2-5.4 combined.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The engineering combination is sensible but each piece is established: groupwise min-max quantization with scale/bias metadata (Eq. 3) is standard, split-depth residual reuse is explicitly attributed to CoMem and disclaimed as new (Section 2, Table 11), and the KV block sharing that produces the 54.5% allocator reduction is attributed to PagedAttention. The genuinely new increment is accounting for the whole hybrid entry rather than the residual alone, plus the ForkAudit ownership harness. The capacity number is real and useful but is one operating point on one model, two datasets, 60 items, one hardware family, one split depth. The most transferable idea - that output and terminal-state equality can pass while a persistent base is corrupted - is demonstrated on exactly one retrospective defect, which the paper correctly refuses to generalize. ForkAudit itself is a validation harness rather than new knowledge, and it is demonstrated on a configuration other than the one the paper measures, so even its practical significance for Q-CoMem is unestablished. Narrow and incremental for ICLR, with uncertain significance beyond this specific stack.

paper_summary: The paper proposes Q-CoMem, a capacity-first extension of CoMem split replay for hybrid (attention + gated-delta-network) LLMs. An offline Write runs a document to split depth j, then groupwise-quantizes the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer full-attention KV and lower-layer convolution/recurrent state; an online Read dequantizes that entry, shares immutable document tensors, creates request-local mutable state via copy-on-write and recurrent rebinding, replays the query through layers [0,j), and reconstructs the suffix through [j,L). The stated framing is that retained document state is the one term of a device-memory budget (Eq. 1) that scales with the hot document set, so the paper trades suffix computation for retained bytes. On a 60-item archival Qasper/2WikiMQA validation cohort with Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on H20-3e, a frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 policy reduces mean retained payload from 136.235 to 9.661 MiB/document (14.10x) at a paired mean-F1 difference of -0.39 points (95% bootstrap [-2.04, 1.08]). A separate 8-item execution (indices 6-9, a subset of the 60) reports the adverse latency side: TTFT rises from 0.163 s to about 0.673 s and generated-token throughput falls from 13.38 to 7.15-7.19 tok/s, while TPOT stays within 2.5%. The paper pairs this with ForkAudit, a fail-closed seven-target ownership trace over a 96-configuration KV-by-GDN factorial, which reports a 54.5% post-priming allocator-delta reduction from shared-document KV at N=32 and reproduces one historical alias that corrupted a persistent base while tokens and terminal request state stayed exact. The paper explicitly disclaims lower total process memory, measured recall, edge performance, TTFT acceleration, and broad quality preservation.
strongest_verified_contribution: The retained-state decomposition and its measurement: Eq. 2 counts the boundary residual plus lower-layer attention KV plus lower-layer convolution/recurrent state as one denominator, and Table 1 then separates the two sources of reduction that are usually conflated - splitting removes the upper-layer entry (136.235 -> 34.683 MiB/doc, 3.93x) and quantization shrinks what the lower layers must keep (34.683 -> 9.661 MiB/doc), for 14.10x overall at a measured mean-F1 change of -0.39 points with a reported interval that the paper explicitly refuses to read as equivalence. Reporting the adverse latency consequence of that same design point in a separate, clearly labelled table (TTFT 0.163 -> ~0.673 s, throughput 13.38 -> ~7.19 tok/s) rather than omitting it is the part of this paper I would most want other systems papers to copy.
strengths: Claim calibration is excellent and rare. The abstract enumerates what is NOT claimed ('We do not claim lower total process memory, measured recall, edge-device performance, or broad quality preservation'), Section 5.6 restates the boundary, and Appendix H expands it. Every headline number I recomputed from the tables reproduces exactly, including the audit's count factorizations (20,992x10 = 209,920 attention calls; 20,992x30 + 192x30 = 635,520 GDN calls; 540 = (1+8)x60; 480 = 8x60).

The experiments are organized so a reader can find each result type without hunting. Section 5 opens with a one-sentence roadmap ('Section 5.2 reports the capacity result the method targets, Section 5.3 the online cost it pays, and Section 5.4 the answer quality it retains'), and the subsection titles are literally 'Memory: retained state per document', 'Latency: TTFT, TPOT, and throughput', and 'Answer quality'. This is exactly right and I found each number on the first attempt.

The Motivation-to-Methodology link is one of the cleanest I have seen in a systems paper. Section 3's three run-in headers ('Retained document state is the controllable term' / 'Neither endpoint gives a small S(D) at usable warm latency' / 'In a hybrid model the entry is not just larger - it is mutable') form a single argument, and Section 3's closing sentence forward-maps each clause to a specific subsection (4.1-4.2, 4.3, 4.4). Read as topic sentences alone, Sections 1, 3 and 4 do carry one line of reasoning.

Adverse results are surfaced rather than buried: TTFT is roughly 4x worse than exact caching, throughput nearly halves, the aggressive mixed policy has five of 60 items crossing the catastrophic threshold, uniform Q4 loses 3.047 F1, and the 60-item run is admitted (p.8) not to be a source-frozen regeneration.

Memory denominators are explicitly separated into three named estimands (component-sum Store, byte-range-union Store, post-priming allocator delta) and the paper repeatedly refuses to pool or add them (Sections 5.1, 5.2, 5.6). The discipline is right even where, as I note below, the execution is incomplete.

Figures 1 and 2 are well designed, correctly captioned, legible at letter print size, and both are cited from the body. Figure 2's separation of retained-state bit widths from the unchanged BF16 model weights and forward compute directly forestalls the most likely misreading of a quantization paper.
questions: Was the Q4/Q4/Q8 quantized Read path of Section 4.3 ever executed under ForkAudit? Table 3 lists 'vLLM fused attention; BF16/Q16; page 128' and no split depth, which reads as though the primary 96-configuration factorial contains no quantized split-replay execution at all. If so, please say so in Section 5.1 and in the abstract.

What is the component-wise breakdown of the 9.661 MiB/document entry at j=7 - residual versus lower attention KV versus lower GDN convolution/recurrent state - and does it reproduce Eq. 2 from the stated shapes and bit widths?

Why does the same nominal 'Full-prefix Q16/BF16' baseline measure 136.235 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 140.34 MiB/doc in Table 2? Which of the two denominators is conservative, and what accounts for the 4.1 MiB gap?

Are Table 1's 'Q-CoMem same-memory mixed' (9.395 MiB) and Table 2's 'Q-CoMem per-layer mixed' (9.74 MiB) the same policy? Section 4.2 describes one per-layer policy with bits [8,8,4,4,8,8,8]; Figure 2(b) shows [8,8,8,4,8,8,8] for the frozen policy. Please confirm which vector belongs to which row of which table.

What metric is 'Recall'? It appears in both main-table headers and in ten disclaimers but is never defined. Is it retrieval recall over evidence paragraphs, LongBench answer recall, or something else?

In Section 5.5, 'token equality catches 0/5 of the semantic-complete mutants and exact logits catch 1/5' - which campaign is this? It follows a sentence naming the five designer-executor-separated controls, but Table 9 shows HF04 changing both tokens and logits, so the designer-executor token catch is 1/5. Please name the cohort at the point of the statistic.
Section 5.1 never states the split depth. Is j=7 (from Figure 2's caption) used for every Q-CoMem row of Tables 1 and 2, and was j held fixed across both cohorts?

Table 5 lists 'SGLang 0.5.17 cache off/on plus 24 fixed-configuration HYPIC timing/quality cells' for the matched serving controls, while Tables 18 and 19 state the HYPIC rows run on SGLang 0.5.14. Which version applies to which cells?
Table 2 reports medians over three timing repeats. What is the spread across those repeats, and does the ~0.001 s separation among the four Q-CoMem TTFT values (0.673/0.674/0.673/0.674) exceed it?

Table 15 shows 'Paged-prefix baseline' and 'Audited hybrid fork' with identical Final (2.229 GiB) and Peak (2.843 GiB). What does the borrowed-GDN ownership mechanism contribute on its own, given that the 54.5% reduction appears attributable entirely to shared-document KV?

issues.location: Section 5.5 'Ownership-audit cohort and procedure' (p.7, lines 363-368); Table 3 (p.14); Section 3 third paragraph (p.3-4); Sections 4.3-4.4 (p.5); Abstract (p.1); Appendix H (p.27)
issues.observed_evidence: Section 5.5 states the audited configuration is 'ten vLLM-0.26 Triton full-attention layers with BF16 KV (the protocol's "Q16" storage label, not quantization) and 128-token pages, plus thirty Transformers-torch GDN layers', with PG-19 4,095-token documents, a 32-token registered transition, N in {1,8,32}, and 8 argmax outputs. Table 3 confirms: 'KV backend: vLLM fused attention; BF16/Q16; page 128' and 'Document / query: 4,095 / 32 tokens; PG-19 train only'. Nothing in Section 5.5 or Table 3 mentions a split depth j, a boundary residual, a dequantization step, or Qasper/2WikiMQA. By contrast Tables 1 and 2 measure a j=7 quantized Q4/Q4/Q8 split-replay path on Qasper/2WikiMQA under Transformers. The only signal that these differ is Appendix H's phrase 'one page size, 16-bit KV', 27 pages in. Meanwhile the abstract asserts 'A fail-closed FORKAUDIT trace validates immutability, copy-on-write, recurrent rebinding, and call provenance' immediately after describing the Q-CoMem Read path, and Section 3's third paragraph presents hybrid mutability as the reason Sections 4.3 and 4.4 exist.
issues.why_it_matters: This is precisely the structural failure my lens is asked to test for. The paper's argument is Motivation (retained state is the controllable term; the hybrid entry is mutable, so sharing is an ownership question) -> Methodology (Section 4.3 forks the dequantized entry under an ownership discipline; Section 4.4 validates that discipline) -> Experiments (Section 5.5 reports whether the discipline holds). The first two links hold. The third does not: Section 5.5 tests a different artifact from the one Section 4.3 describes and from the one Sections 5.2-5.4 measure. So the Experiments section is not one story with the Methodology - it is two, and the seam is invisible unless the reader collates a sentence on p.7 with a table on p.14 and a clause on p.27. Because the abstract and Section 1's third contribution bullet couple ForkAudit to Q-CoMem without qualification, a reader will reasonably conclude the shipped quantized path has been ownership-audited. On the evidence in this PDF, it has not.
issues.required_fix: State the scope gap explicitly in three places. (1) In Section 5.1, add a short table or paragraph mapping each results table (1, 2, 15) to the exact executed system: model, runtime, KV backend, split depth, quantization policy, dataset. (2) In Section 5.5's first sentence, say plainly that the primary factorial runs BF16/Q16 KV with no split residual and therefore audits the ownership discipline, not the quantized Read path. (3) In the abstract, either qualify the ForkAudit sentence ('on a BF16-KV configuration of the same ownership design') or, preferably, run the seven-target contract on the Q4/Q4/Q8 configuration of Table 1 and report that verdict. Add the gap to Section 5.6 as a named limitation.
issues.verification_test: Hand the revised main text to a reader who has not seen the appendix and ask: 'Was the Q4/Q4/Q8 configuration reported in Table 1 ever passed through ForkAudit, yes or no?' The revision passes only if the reader answers correctly from Sections 5.1-5.5 alone, without consulting Table 3 or Appendix H. Additionally, a diff of the stated configurations for Table 1, Table 2 and Table 15 should surface every axis on which they differ.
issues.evidence_needed: Either a ForkAudit execution on the quantized split-replay Read path with the seven-target coverage/verdict table for that exact configuration, or an explicit, prominently placed statement that the quantized path is unaudited and that the ownership result transfers only by design argument.

issues.location: Table 1 (p.6) vs Table 2 (p.7); Section 5.1 'Memory denominators' (p.6, lines 294-301); Section 5.2 (p.6); Abstract (p.1)
issues.observed_evidence: The same nominal baseline row, 'Full-prefix Q16/BF16', is 136.235 MiB/doc in Table 1 and 140.34 MiB/doc in Table 2 - a 3.0% gap on the denominator of every compression claim in the paper. Section 5.1 acknowledges that 'the accounting implementations differ' (component sum of packed residual data, scales, biases and unique lower-cache tensor storage, versus the physical byte-range union owned by one retained entry) but gives no worked example, no reconciliation, and no statement of which is conservative. The two Q-CoMem Q4/Q4/Q8 rows likewise disagree: 9.661 MiB (Table 1) versus 10.01 MiB (Table 2). A third denominator, the post-priming allocator delta in GiB, appears in Section 5.5 and Table 15.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the 'would a reader confuse two different memory denominators?' question, and the answer is yes. The abstract's headline is 14.10x; the same design point in Table 2 is 92.87%, i.e. 14.02x, against a 3% larger baseline. A reader cannot tell how much of any inter-table difference is method and how much is accounting, and the paper never quantifies the accounting gap even once. Separating denominators without ever reconciling them converts a transparency virtue into an unresolvable ambiguity: the reader is warned not to pool the numbers but is given no basis for interpreting either.
issues.required_fix: Add one reconciliation: take a single retained entry from the same configuration, compute both denominators on it, and report both values with the delta and its source (Python/shape metadata, padding, alignment, shared storage counted once versus byte-range union, etc.) in a two-row table or a three-sentence paragraph in Section 5.1. Annotate every compression ratio in the paper with the denominator that produced it (e.g. '14.10x [component]' and '92.87% [byte-range]'). State which denominator is the conservative bound on deployed bytes.
issues.verification_test: Instrument one Q4/Q4/Q8 entry at j=7 under both accountings in the same process and confirm the reported delta. Then confirm that a reader can state, for each headline ratio in the abstract and Sections 5.2-5.4, which denominator it uses, from the surrounding text alone.
issues.evidence_needed: A single-entry dual-denominator measurement plus a per-component breakdown (residual / attention KV / GDN state) at j=7 that sums to the reported 9.661 and 10.01 MiB values under their respective accountings.

issues.location: Section 5.5, all four paragraphs (pp.7-8, lines 363-424); Section 5.5 'Falsification beyond output equality' (p.8, lines 412-418); Tables 8 and 9 (pp.19)
issues.observed_evidence: Section 5.5 is the longest subsection of Section 5 - roughly 1.9 pages against under 1.0 page for Sections 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 combined - and contains no main-text table or figure; all fourteen supporting tables sit in the appendix. Its 'Ownership evidence' paragraph is a continuous count cascade: 'yielding 8x3x6 = 144 selected-owner-row checks, 8x3x540 = 12,960 full serializer/live-object rows, 8x480 = 3,840 direct clone edges, and 8x3 = 24 stable artifacts. Here 60 = 30x2 denotes persistent layer/family coordinates and 480 = 8x60 direct clone destinations, while each phase contains the full 540 = (1+8)x60 serializer-row universe with six owner-row anchors.' The single finding the abstract leads with - the historical alias invisible to output equality - appears as one clause inside the fourth paragraph. In that same paragraph, 'token equality catches 0/5 of the semantic-complete mutants and exact logits catch 1/5' follows two sentences after 'five designer-executor-separated constructed controls', but the statistic actually describes the target-gate-suppression M-series (Table 8, where M1/M2/M5/M6/M7 complete and only M5 changes logits). Table 9's designer-executor series has HF04 changing both tokens and logits, i.e. a 1/5 token catch, so the natural reading of the sentence is wrong.
issues.why_it_matters: The audit is the paper's most distinctive component, and its presentation makes it effectively unreviewable in the main text. The counts are arithmetically correct (I checked all of them) but carry no interpretive weight for a reader who cannot see what a 'serializer row' or a 'clone edge' is; they read as volume rather than evidence. Simultaneously, the two results that would actually change a reader's mind - a historical defect that output equality misses, and a seven-target pass/fail verdict - are compressed to clauses. The ambiguous '0/5' antecedent then misassigns a falsification statistic across two different fault campaigns, which is a factual clarity error in the paper's central negative-control claim, not merely awkward writing.
issues.required_fix: Restructure Section 5.5 into two clearly separated paragraphs: 'what the audit checks' (the seven targets, one sentence each) and 'what it found' (verdicts, the allocator endpoints, the historical alias). Promote a compact version of Table 6 (seven targets x coverage x verdict) into the main text as the anchor. Move the entire count cascade, including the 60/480/540 identities, into Appendix D. Attach an explicit cohort name to every fraction: 'in the target-gate-suppression campaign (Table 8), token equality catches 0 of the 5 semantics-completing mutants and exact logits catch 1 of 5.' Give the historical-alias result its own run-in header, since the abstract promises it.
issues.verification_test: Ask a reader who has read only Section 5.5 two questions: 'Which fault campaign did token equality fail to catch, and how many of how many?' and 'What did ForkAudit find that output comparison could not?' Both must be answerable correctly and unambiguously. Separately, confirm that no fraction in Section 5.5 can be attached to more than one table.
issues.evidence_needed: None beyond the existing appendix tables; this is a reorganization and disambiguation of material already present.

issues.location: Table 1 rows (p.6); Table 2 rows (p.7); Section 4.2 (p.5, lines 216-218); Figure 2(b) (p.4); Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.4
issues.observed_evidence: The two main tables share only three of six rows. Table 1: dense / full-prefix Q16 / split Q16 / frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 / same-memory mixed / aggressive mixed. Table 2: dense / full-prefix Q16 / Q8 / Q4/Q4/Q8 / per-layer mixed / Q4. What appears to be one policy is named four ways - 'same-memory mixed' (Table 1), 'per-layer mixed' (Table 2), 'same-memory per-layer mixed precision' (Section 5.1), 'the calibrated per-layer point' (Sections 5.2 and 5.4) - with two different Store values (9.395 and 9.74 MiB). Compounding this, Section 4.2 states the per-layer policy uses 'active-layer widths [8, 8, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8]', while Figure 2(b), captioned 'Frozen policy', displays a per-layer bit row of 8 8 8 4 8 8 8 over layer indices 0-6. Two near-identical seven-element vectors, differing only at position 2, belong to two different policies, and neither is labelled with the policy name in the figure. Table 1's dense row shows Store as '-' while Table 2's shows '0.00' for the same quantity.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's stated organizing logic is that memory, latency and quality are measured separately for the same design point. That only works if the reader can line the design points up across tables, and here they cannot without inference. A reader tracking 'the per-layer mixed policy' from Section 4.2 through Figure 2 to Tables 1 and 2 encounters four names, two Store values, and two confusable bit vectors, and has no way to confirm they are following one thing. This directly defeats the memory-latency-quality separation the paper is built on.
issues.required_fix: Introduce one policy-naming table early in Section 5.1: canonical name, bit assignment per state type and per layer, calibration source, and which of Tables 1/2/18 it appears in. Use the canonical name everywhere, including table rows. Label Figure 2(b)'s bit row explicitly as the per-layer widths implied by the frozen state-type policy, and add the contrasting per-layer-mixed vector beside it or drop the numeric row from the figure entirely. Make the dense-recompute Store representation identical in both tables. Where a policy appears in only one table, say why in the caption.
issues.verification_test: Give a reader the string 'per-layer mixed' and ask them to name its bit vector and its Store value in each cohort. The revision passes only if there is exactly one correct answer per cohort and the reader finds both without backtracking.
issues.evidence_needed: None; requires renaming and one cross-reference table.

issues.location: Section 5.1 'Quality cohort' and 'Latency execution' (pp.5-6); Table 1 caption (p.6); Table 2 caption (p.7); Figure 2 caption (p.4); Eq. 2 (p.4)

issues.location: Abstract (p.1, lines 031-033); Section 5.5 'Allocator reduction with canonical equality' (p.8); Table 15 (p.22); Section 2 'Paged and prefix-aware inference' (p.3)
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract states 'Separately, shared-document KV lowers the post-priming allocated delta from 4.901 to 2.229 GiB at N = 32'. Table 15 shows the four endpoints: Full-copy KV/Materialized GDN = 4.901, Full-copy KV/Borrowed GDN = 4.890, Shared-doc KV/Materialized GDN ('Paged-prefix baseline') = 2.229, Shared-doc KV/Borrowed GDN ('Audited hybrid fork') = 2.229. Final and Peak are identical (2.229 / 2.843) for the last two rows; only the generation increment differs (0.019 vs 1.950), which Section 5.5 correctly characterizes as an allocation-timing change. So the entire 54.5% reduction is produced by KV block sharing, which the paper itself attributes to PagedAttention in Section 2, and the borrowed-GDN ownership mechanism - the actually novel part - contributes nothing to the final or peak allocator figure.
issues.why_it_matters: This number is one of four quantitative results in the abstract, sits immediately beside the paper's own contributions, and is the only GiB-scale figure in the paper. The word 'Separately' is the sole cue that it does not come from Q-CoMem's novel mechanism. The paper's technical statements are accurate and its Table 15 is honest, but the abstract's placement invites exactly the misattribution the rest of the paper works hard to prevent, and it inflates the apparent contribution relative to what the ownership design itself buys.
issues.required_fix: In the abstract, attribute the reduction to KV block sharing explicitly and note that it is measured under a third denominator distinct from Store. In Section 5.5, add one sentence stating what the borrowed-GDN arm contributes on its own (per Table 15: no change in final or peak allocated bytes; a shift of ~1.93 GiB of allocation from setup to generation time), so the reader sees the ownership mechanism's own allocator cost-benefit rather than only the shared-KV headline.
issues.verification_test: Read the abstract's four quantitative claims and ask, for each, 'which mechanism in this paper produced it?' Every answer must be unambiguous from the abstract sentence alone. The 54.5% claim currently fails this test.
issues.evidence_needed: None; Table 15 already contains the disaggregation. This is an attribution and placement fix.

issues.location: Table 1 (p.6), TTFT and Recall columns; Table 2 (p.7), Recall column; ten 'Recall' mentions across pp.1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 27

If Recall is genuinely retained as a target metric for future work, define it on first use (one clause: which recall, over what). issues.location: Figure 3 and Appendix C (p.13); Tables 3 and 4 (p.14); Table 5 caption (p.14)

Tables 3 and 4 are likewise never cited by number and have no introductory prose; Appendix C consists of a heading, an uncited figure occupying roughly half of page 13 with the remainder blank, two uncited tables on page 14, one orphan paragraph about anchor field order, and then Table 5. Table 5's caption is typeset at a different, narrower indentation than every other caption in the paper and visually collides with the end of the preceding paragraph ('...their source anchor.' running into 'Table 5: Cohort-to-claim authorization'). issues.why_it_matters: An uncited figure has no established role in the argument, so a reader cannot tell what it is meant to establish or where it belongs; the same applies to two uncited tables presented with no prose at all. The Table 5 caption collision is a visible typesetting defect on a page the reader will reach. Together these make Appendix C read as an unsorted dump rather than a section.
issues.required_fix: Cite Figure 3 from Section 4.4 or 5.5 and Tables 3 and 4 from Section 5.5, each with a one-sentence lead-in stating what the reader should take from it. Fix the Table 5 caption to use the standard caption environment and margin. Either retitle Appendix C to cover its actual contents or split the cohort-authorization and trace-verdict tables into their own subsection. Reflow page 13 so Figure 3 is not followed by half a blank page.
issues.verification_test: Grep the compiled text for every 'Figure N' and 'Table N': each must appear at least once outside its own caption. Visually inspect pages 13-14 at 100% for caption alignment and whitespace.

issues.location: Table 4 caption (p.14); Appendix A (p.12, 'QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116'); Appendix I / Table 27 (pp.29-31)

The job/trial ID and the round-numbered paths do not name the authors and I do not read them as breaking double-blind, but they expose an internal iteration process (including a 'round32_input.pdf' fed to a fault designer) that a reviewer will notice and that serves no reader. issues.location: Section 4.2 (p.4, line 192); Tables 1-2 row labels (pp.6-7); Section 5.5 (p.7, line 364); Table 3 'KV backend' (p.14); Table 18 footnote (p.24); Figure 1 'Q-CoMem Store' (p.2) vs Store column headers
issues.observed_evidence: 'Q16' carries at least three distinct senses: a numeric format ('Q16 is the BF16 unpacked reference', Section 4.2; 'Q16 denotes BF16', Table 18 footnote), a baseline system name ('Full-prefix Q16/BF16', 'Q-CoMem split Q16/BF16' as table rows, and 'split Q16' as the bootstrap comparator throughout Section 5.4), and a storage label in the audit protocol that the paper explicitly says is not quantization ('BF16 KV (the protocol's "Q16" storage label, not quantization)', Section 5.5; 'BF16/Q16', Table 3). It also appears as a bit width inside a policy specification ('a Q4 residual, Q16 projections', Section 4.2). Separately, 'Store' names both a system component (Figure 1's cylinder is labelled 'Q-CoMem Store') and a metric (the 'Store (MiB/doc)' column of every results table).
issues.why_it_matters: The paper asks the reader to track a term that means a numeric format, a baseline configuration, a non-quantized storage label, and a per-component bit width, sometimes within one sentence. 'Store' as both an artifact and a metric compounds this. Both overloads are disclosed somewhere, but disclosure spread across four locations does not prevent the confusion; it just makes it the reader's job.
issues.required_fix: Reserve 'Q16' for one meaning. I suggest dropping it as a format name in favour of 'BF16', keeping 'full-prefix BF16' as the baseline row name, and renaming the audit protocol's storage label to something that cannot be read as a bit width. Rename Figure 1's component to 'Q-CoMem entry store' or keep 'Store' strictly as the metric. Add a two-line terminology note at the end of Section 4 fixing Store, retained state, allocator delta, split replay and the audit component.
issues.verification_test: For each occurrence of 'Q16' and 'Store' in the revised manuscript, confirm a single referent is recoverable from the sentence alone without consulting another section.

issues.location: Section 1 paragraphs 2-3 (p.1-2) vs Section 3 paragraphs 2-3 (p.3-4); relative lengths of Sections 5.2-5.4 vs 5.5 (pp.6-8)
issues.observed_evidence: Section 1's second paragraph ('Dense recomputation and exact prefix caching form the two endpoints. The former stores no document state but repeatedly processes the prefix; the latter gives low warm TTFT but retains the complete prefix cache') and Section 3's second paragraph ('Dense recomputation sets S(D) = 0 but pays full prefill on every query. Exact prefix caching is the low-TTFT reference point, but it retains per-document state at every layer') make the same argument. Section 1's third paragraph and Section 3's third paragraph likewise both establish hybrid mutability. Section 1 plus Section 3 occupy roughly 2.2 of 9 main-text pages. By contrast Sections 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 - the memory, latency and quality results the abstract leads with - together occupy under one page, less than Section 5.5 alone.
issues.why_it_matters: Read as topic sentences, Sections 1 and 3 are one argument stated twice, and the page budget is allocated inversely to the paper's own stated priorities. Space spent restating the motivation is space not spent on the per-component Store breakdown, the timing dispersion, or the denominator reconciliation that this review asks for elsewhere - all of which would fit in the reclaimed page.
issues.required_fix: Compress Section 1 to problem statement, one-sentence approach, and contributions, letting Section 3 carry the endpoint and mutability arguments once with Eq. 1. Reallocate the recovered space to Sections 5.2-5.4: add the per-component retained-state breakdown, the timing spread across the three repeats, and the denominator reconciliation.
issues.verification_test: Extract the topic sentence of every paragraph in Sections 1 and 3 and check that no two assert the same proposition. Then confirm Sections 5.2-5.4 together occupy at least as much main text as Section 5.5.

issues.location: Whole manuscript (no LLM-use disclosure found); Appendix B Ethics Statement (p.13); Reference 'Liu et al., 2026a' (p.10)
issues.observed_evidence: I searched the full text and found no LLM-use disclosure anywhere in the 31 pages, which ICLR 2026 requires where LLM use is significant. The Ethics Statement is placed in Appendix B (p.13) rather than immediately after the main text, though a Reproducibility Statement is correctly placed before the references. The CoMem reference (Liu et al., 2026a, COLM 2026 Workshop on Efficient Reasoning) lists 'Key' and 'Rayying' among its authors - these are evidently online handles rather than personal names, appearing in a formal venue citation. Format and page limit are otherwise compliant: the ICLR 2026 template is used, main text runs Sections 1-6 plus the Reproducibility Statement and ends on page 9 with references beginning on the same page, and the submission is properly anonymized ('Anonymous authors / Paper under double-blind review').
issues.why_it_matters: The missing LLM disclosure is a venue-compliance gap that is trivially fixable but is checked at submission. The pseudonymous author entries in a cited reference are a citation-integrity blemish that a reviewer notices immediately and that reflects on the care taken with the bibliography, which in this paper carries the load of positioning against seven prior systems.
issues.required_fix: Add the required LLM-use disclosure. Move the Ethics Statement to follow Section 6 before the Reproducibility Statement, per the template's ordering. Correct or remove the pseudonymous entries in the CoMem reference, or cite the venue record's canonical author list.
issues.verification_test: Run the ICLR 2026 submission checklist: template, 9-page main text, anonymity, reproducibility statement placement, ethics statement placement, LLM disclosure present. Spot-check every reference's author list against its venue record.

ethics_concerns: No ethics concerns warranting a flag. The paper includes an Ethics Statement (Appendix B) covering the absence of human-subject data, its use of public PG-19, Qasper and 2WikiMQA text, and the dual-use observation that memory efficiency lowers deployment cost while potentially increasing the scale of model use. Datasets are public and standard. My only procedural notes, recorded as minor issues rather than ethics flags, are the absent LLM-use disclosure and the internal platform identifiers (QS Job 234340 / Trial 1830116, round-numbered artifact paths) that appear in the appendices; these do not name the authors and I do not read them as breaking double-blind review.

The model read the submission PDF at snapshot 3245a5de0899448e0aa73c978bffd18465740fac5257a3559b7bb6a1ad621ce0 via text extraction (pdftotext -layout) across all 31 pages and additionally rendered pages 1-9 and 13-14 for visual inspection of figures, tables, caption placement and page layout. evidence_that_would_raise_score: A ForkAudit execution on the actual Q4/Q4/Q8 quantized split-replay Read path of Section 4.3, with the seven-target coverage and verdict table reported for that exact configuration. This is the single change that would most raise my score, because it would close the Motivation -> Methodology -> Experiments chain that the paper's structure promises but does not currently deliver.

A source-frozen regeneration of the 60-item Store-F1 panel with pre-run full-source and model-weight ledgers, removing the authors' own caveat (p.8) that the headline capacity and quality result cannot be described as fresh source-frozen regeneration.

A single worked reconciliation of the component-sum and byte-range-union Store denominators on one identical retained entry, plus a per-component breakdown at the stated split depth that reproduces 34.683 and 9.661 MiB/document from Eq. 2.

Timing evidence beyond eight items, with dispersion across the three repeats reported rather than medians alone, and ideally a second document-length setting so the reader can see how the TTFT penalty scales with the suffix work.

A rewritten Section 5.5 with a compact seven-target verdict table in the main text, the count cascade relocated to Appendix D, and every falsification fraction bound to a named campaign - which would let a reviewer actually assess the paper's most distinctive component.
A second model family or a second hardware stack for the capacity result, even at reduced item count, to show the 14.10x is not specific to this one Qwen3.5/H20 configuration.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Confirmation that the primary ownership factorial contains no split-replay or quantized execution at all, making the Section 3 -> Section 4.3 -> Section 5.5 chain unsupported by any executed Q-CoMem run rather than merely under-disclosed.

Evidence that Table 1's and Table 2's 'Full-prefix Q16' rows differ in configuration and not only in accounting, which would make 14.10x and 92.87% non-comparable and undermine the paper's central compression framing.
Any indication that the eight-item indices-6-9 timing slice was chosen after inspecting results rather than pre-registered, given that it is a subset of the same 60 items used for the quality claim.

Failure to reproduce the historical-alias case study from the archived pre-fix source, since that single retrospective defect is the sole empirical support for the paper's claim that output equality can miss state aliasing.

Discovery that the per-layer mixed policy's calibration set overlaps the validation items, which would invalidate the Table 1 and Table 2 rows for that policy and cast doubt on the 'frozen before validation' framing used throughout.
review_limitations: PDF-only access. I could not inspect the LaTeX source, the evidence packages, the experiment registry, or any artifact referenced in Table 27, so every reproducibility and provenance judgment here rests solely on what the manuscript asserts about itself.

My assigned lens is clarity and presentation. I verified all arithmetic and cross-references I could check from the printed values, but I did not independently assess the correctness of the gated-delta-network recurrence, the quantization error analysis, or the storage-witness interval algebra of Appendix D beyond checking internal consistency.

I am not able to judge whether the ForkAudit trusted computing base as described is adequate for the ownership claims it supports; a reviewer with systems-verification expertise should evaluate Section 4.4's TCB statement and Appendix D's overlap test.
The historical-alias finding, the paper's most interesting negative result, rests on artifacts I cannot access; I have taken the paper's description of it at face value while noting that it is n=1.
I read the paper on its own merits with no knowledge of prior review rounds or author responses, as instructed.
